subject: Physics
content: Transverse and longitudinal waves: Students should be able to describe the differences between transverse and longitudinal waves. In a transverse wave, the oscillations are perpendicular to the direction of energy transfer.

subject: Physics
content: Properties of electromagnetic waves: Students should be able to explain how the colour of a surface affects the emission, absorption, and reflection of infrared radiation.

subject: Physics
content: Investigating infrared radiation: Students should be able to describe methods to investigate how different surfaces emit and absorb infrared radiation.

subject: Physics
content: Pressure and pressure differences in fluids: Students should know and be able to use the relationship between pressure, force, and area: pressure = force / area.

subject: Physics
content: Distance and displacement: Students should be able to explain the difference between distance and displacement and determine displacement using scale diagrams.

subject: Physics
content: Resultant forces: Students should be able to calculate the resultant of two or more forces acting along the same line.

subject: Physics
content: Newton's First Law: Students should understand the concept of inertia and how forces affect the motion of an object.

subject: Physics
content: Velocity and acceleration: Students should be able to interpret and draw distance-time and velocity-time graphs, and calculate acceleration.

subject: Physics
content: Atmospheric pressure: Students should understand how atmospheric pressure varies with height above the Earth's surface.

subject: Physics
content: Forces and moments: Students should be able to describe how moments can be increased and calculate the size of a moment.

subject: Physics
content: Momentum: Students should know and use the equation for momentum: momentum = mass × velocity.

subject: Physics
content: Stopping distance: Students should understand the factors affecting stopping distances, including thinking distance and braking distance.

subject: Physics
content: Energy transfers during braking: Students should be able to explain why the temperature of the brakes increases during braking.

subject: Physics
content: Properties of waves: Students should understand how sound waves are detected and how microphones convert sound waves into electrical signals.

subject: Physics
content: Permanent and induced magnetism: Students should be able to describe the properties of permanent and induced magnets.

subject: Physics
content: Magnetic fields: Students should understand the concept of magnetic fields and the motor effect.

subject: Physics
content: Electromagnetic induction: Students should be able to explain how a direct current can be induced in a coil and the factors affecting the size of the induced current.

subject: Physics
content: Sound waves and human hearing: Students should understand how age and exposure to loud sounds can affect human hearing.

subject: Physics
content: Conservation of momentum: Students should understand the concept of a closed system and apply the conservation of momentum to collisions.

subject: Physics
content: Newton's Third Law: Students should understand and apply Newton's Third Law to interactions between objects.

subject: Physics
content: Force and momentum: Students should be able to use the relationship between force, change in momentum, and time taken: force = change in momentum / time taken.

subject: Physics
content: Changes in momentum and safety: Students should understand how safety features in vehicles, such as flexible bumpers, reduce injury by increasing the time of impact.

subject: Physics
content: Equations of motion: Students should be able to use the equations of motion to calculate velocity, acceleration, and distance travelled.

subject: Physics
content: Orbits of planets and satellites: Students should know the types of objects that orbit planets and understand the forces acting on them.

subject: Physics
content: Wave speed: Students should know and use the equation for wave speed: wave speed = frequency × wavelength.

subject: Physics
content: Gravitational fields: Students should understand the effect of gravitational forces on the motion of objects in orbit.

subject: Physics
content: Red-shift: Students should understand how the red-shift of light from galaxies provides evidence for the Big Bang theory and the expansion of the Universe.

subject: Physics
content: Reflection of waves: Students should understand the law of reflection and the difference between specular and diffuse reflection.

subject: Physics
content: Refraction of waves: Students should understand the concept of refraction and explain why it occurs at the boundary between two different media.

subject: Physics
content: Transformers: Students should understand the structure and function of transformers, including the material used for the core and why.

subject: Physics
content: Transformer equations: Students should be able to use the transformer equations to calculate current, voltage, and power in primary and secondary coils.
